forms: order pictures from smallest to largest
which comes first or last in the order
which object is out of order
MATH.G3.NUMBER.NUMBER_CONCEPT.ORDER_BY_S.mastery: The child arranges three to six real objects or pictures from the smallest to the largest and from the largest to the smallest, says which is first and last in the order, and keeps to the size asked for (length, height or bulk), not colour or position.
MATH.G3.NUMBER.NUMBER_CONCEPT.ORDER_BY_S.hands_on: Arranging real objects collected from the school compound is done in class.

forms: which position is the object in
point to the object in a position
who is just before or after
MATH.G3.NUMBER.NUMBER_CONCEPT.ORDINAL_PO.mastery: Given a line of up to 20 objects or people and a reference point (the front, the left), the child names the position of any one of them (the 7th) and points to the one in a named position, counting from the stated end.

MATH.G3.NUMBER.NUMBER_CONCEPT.WRITE_ORDI.mastery: The child writes a position from 1st to 20th in symbols (1st, 2nd, 3rd, 4th ... 20th) with the right ending, and in words (first, second, third, twelfth, twentieth) with the right spelling, and matches the two forms.

forms: count on in ones from a number
what comes next after a hundred
MATH.G3.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.COUNT_FORWA.mastery: Starting from any number up to 1,000, the child counts on in ones, tens or hundreds, crossing a ten or a hundred correctly (198, 199, 200; 390, 400, 410), and says the next three numbers.

forms: missing hundred in a backward line
MATH.G3.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.COUNT_BACK_.mastery: The child counts back from 1,000 in hundreds (1,000, 900, 800 ... 100) and from any hundred, and says the hundred before a given hundred.

forms: name the place of a digit
write hundreds, tens and ones as a number
MATH.G3.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.PLACE_VALUE.mastery: For any number up to 999 the child names the place of each digit (hundreds, tens, ones), says what each digit is worth (the 4 in 347 is 40), builds the number from hundreds, tens and ones including an empty place (3 hundreds and 5 ones is 305), and compares numbers by their hundreds first.

forms: match a number to its name
read a price or a page number
MATH.G3.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.READ_SYMBOL.mastery: The child reads aloud any number up to 1,000 written in symbols, saying the hundreds, the 'and' and the tens and ones (406 is four hundred and six), and picks the number said from a list.

forms: write the words as a number
MATH.G3.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.WORDS_100.mastery: The child writes any number up to 100 in words with the correct spelling (forty, not fourty; a hyphen in twenty-seven) and writes a number given in words in symbols.

MATH.G3.NUMBER.WHOLE_NUMBERS.PATTERNS_10.mastery: The child finds the rule of a pattern that goes up or down in ones, twos, fives, tens or hundreds (240, 250, 260, __), fills in missing numbers in the middle or at the end, and makes a pattern of their own. Number games with patterns are done in class.

forms: a word story with a total
fill in the missing digit of the sum
MATH.G3.NUMBER.ADDITION.ADD_3D_2D_NO_REG.mastery: The child adds a 3-digit number and a 1- or 2-digit number with no carrying (342 + 25, 604 + 3), lining up ones under ones in a column and also working across, with sums up to 1,000. Practice with apparatus or digital games is done in class.

forms: find the mistake in a working
MATH.G3.NUMBER.ADDITION.ADD_3D_2D_REGROU.mastery: The child adds a 3-digit number and a 1- or 2-digit number where the ones (or the tens) make ten or more, carrying one ten (or one hundred) to the next column, as in 347 + 28 = 375, with the sum up to 1,000.

MATH.G3.NUMBER.ADDITION.ADD_3D_3D_NO_REG.mastery: The child adds two 3-digit numbers with no carrying (423 + 361), column by column from the ones, with a sum up to 1,000.

MATH.G3.NUMBER.ADDITION.ADD_3D_3D_REGROU.mastery: The child adds two 3-digit numbers with one carry, from the ones to the tens or from the tens to the hundreds (256 + 318 = 574), with the sum up to 1,000, and writes the carried digit in the right column.

MATH.G3.NUMBER.ADDITION.ADD_PATTERNS_100.mastery: The child continues a pattern made by adding the same number each time (125, 150, 175, __), finds a missing term, names the number added, and makes a pattern of their own up to 1,000.

MATH.G3.NUMBER.SUBTRACTION.SUB_3D_2D_NO_.mastery: The child subtracts a 2-digit number from a 3-digit number where no column needs regrouping (586 - 43), lining up ones under ones, working from the ones, in a column and across.

MATH.G3.NUMBER.SUBTRACTION.SUB_3D_2D_REG.mastery: The child subtracts a 2-digit number from a 3-digit number where one column needs regrouping (352 - 27 = 325), exchanging one ten for ten ones (or one hundred for ten tens) and crossing out to show it.

forms: a story of how many stay
MATH.G3.NUMBER.SUBTRACTION.SUB_3D_3D_REG.mastery: The child subtracts one 3-digit number from another with one regrouping (634 - 218 = 416, where only the ones are regrouped; 708 - 352 = 356, where only the tens are), from the ones to the hundreds, and checks the answer by adding.

MATH.G3.NUMBER.SUBTRACTION.SUB_MISSING_N.mastery: The child finds the missing number in a subtraction sentence (__ - 125 = 340, 563 - __ = 228) or a missing digit in a column, with single regrouping, by using the link between adding and taking away.

forms: what is taken away each time
MATH.G3.NUMBER.SUBTRACTION.SUB_PATTERNS_.mastery: The child continues a pattern that goes down by the same number (950, 900, 850, __), finds a missing term and names what is taken away each time.

MATH.G3.NUMBER.MULTIPLICATION.MULT_REPEA.mastery: The child shows 1 to 5 groups of 4 or 5 with counters, writes the repeated addition (5 + 5 + 5) and the multiplication (3 x 5 = 15), and says which number is the number of groups and which is the size of each group.

MATH.G3.NUMBER.MULTIPLICATION.MULT_1D_BY.mastery: The child gives the product of any two single-digit numbers (7 x 6 = 42) from the multiplication chart or by known facts, solves equal-groups stories (shelves, rows, legs), and knows that 4 x 7 and 7 x 4 are the same.

MATH.G3.NUMBER.MULTIPLICATION.MULT_BY_10.mastery: The child multiplies any single-digit number by 10 (6 x 10 = 60), explains it as that many tens, and solves stories with bundles or packets of 10.

forms: take away groups until none are left
how many times can you take
MATH.G3.NUMBER.DIVISION.DIV_REPEATED_SUB.mastery: The child takes away 4 or 5 at a time from up to 50 objects until none are left, counts how many times, writes it as a repeated subtraction (20 - 5 - 5 - 5 - 5 = 0) and as a division (20 ÷ 5 = 4).

MATH.G3.NUMBER.DIVISION.DIV_2D_BY_1D.mastery: The child divides a 2-digit number by a single-digit number where it goes exactly (42 ÷ 6 = 7), using the times tables backwards, and solves sharing and grouping stories.

MATH.G3.NUMBER.DIVISION.DIV_BY_10.mastery: The child divides a multiple of ten up to 90 by 10 (70 ÷ 10 = 7), explains it as how many tens, and solves packing stories.

MATH.G3.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.FRACTION_OF_WHO.mastery: Given a shape or cut-out folded or cut into 2, 4 or 8 equal parts, the child names one part as 1/2, 1/4 or 1/8, writes it, and says a shape cut into unequal parts does not show halves or quarters.
MATH.G3.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.FRACTION_OF_WHO.hands_on: Folding circular and rectangular cut-outs is done in class.

forms: which cut makes the smallest piece
MATH.G3.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.COMPARE_UNIT_FR.mastery: The child says that of the same whole a half is bigger than a quarter and a quarter bigger than an eighth, because more equal parts make each part smaller, and orders the three.

forms: how many is a half of the group
MATH.G3.NUMBER.FRACTIONS.FRACTION_OF_GRO.mastery: The child divides a group of objects (up to 40) into 2, 4 or 8 equal groups and names one small group as 1/2, 1/4 or 1/8 of the group, and says how many objects that is (1/4 of 12 oranges is 3 oranges).

forms: read a measurement from a picture
MATH.G3.MEASUR.LENGTH.MEASURE_METRES.mastery: The child measures a length or distance in whole metres with a metre stick or a string knotted every metre, starting at one end, laying the stick end to end without gaps or overlaps, and records the result with the unit (6 m).
MATH.G3.MEASUR.LENGTH.MEASURE_METRES.hands_on: Measuring the classroom walls and the compound with metre sticks and knotted strings is done in class.

forms: a story of two pieces joined
MATH.G3.MEASUR.LENGTH.ADD_METRES.mastery: The child adds lengths in metres (the four walls of a classroom: 8 m + 6 m + 8 m + 6 m), in stories and in columns, and writes the total with the unit m.

MATH.G3.MEASUR.LENGTH.SUBTRACT_METRES.mastery: The child finds the difference between two lengths in metres (how much longer the chalkboard is than the table) and what is left when a length is cut off, writing the unit m.

forms: is it more or less than 10 m
MATH.G3.MEASUR.LENGTH.ESTIMATE_METRES.mastery: The child estimates a length or distance up to 10 metres using a body benchmark (a big step is about 1 metre), then measures to check and says whether the estimate was close.
MATH.G3.MEASUR.LENGTH.ESTIMATE_METRES.hands_on: Estimating distances in the compound and checking by measuring is done in class.

forms: read the mass from a balance picture
how many 1 kg masses balance it
MATH.G3.MEASUR.MASS.MEASURE_KG.mastery: The child measures the mass of an object on a beam balance by adding 1 kg masses until the beam is level, reads the mass in whole kilograms, and records it with the unit kg.
MATH.G3.MEASUR.MASS.MEASURE_KG.hands_on: Making 1 kg masses with sand and using a beam balance is done in class.

MATH.G3.MEASUR.MASS.ADD_KG.mastery: The child adds masses in kilograms (a 2 kg bag of sugar and a 5 kg bag of flour), in shop stories and in columns, and writes kg with the total.

MATH.G3.MEASUR.MASS.SUBTRACT_KG.mastery: The child finds the difference between two masses in kilograms (how much heavier) and the mass left after some is used or sold, writing kg.

MATH.G3.MEASUR.MASS.ESTIMATE_KG.mastery: The child holds an object and a 1 kg mass and estimates the object's mass up to 5 kg, says whether it is more or less than 5 kg, then measures on a balance to check.
MATH.G3.MEASUR.MASS.ESTIMATE_KG.hands_on: Estimating by holding items and checking on a balance is done in class.

forms: read a picture of litre jugs
MATH.G3.MEASUR.CAPACITY.MEASURE_LITRES.mastery: The child finds how many litres a container holds by filling it from (or pouring it into) a 1-litre container, counting full litres only and filling each to the top, and records the result with the unit l.
MATH.G3.MEASUR.CAPACITY.MEASURE_LITRES.hands_on: Filling containers with water from a 1-litre container is done in class.

MATH.G3.MEASUR.CAPACITY.ADD_LITRES.mastery: The child adds capacities in litres (5 l of milk in the morning and 3 l in the evening), including the same amount poured again and again, and writes l with the total.

forms: how much more does it hold
MATH.G3.MEASUR.CAPACITY.SUBTRACT_LITRES.mastery: The child finds what is left in a container after some litres are used or poured out, and the difference between two capacities, writing l.

MATH.G3.MEASUR.CAPACITY.ESTIMATE_LITRES.mastery: The child estimates how many litres a container holds, up to 5 litres, using a 1-litre bottle as the benchmark, then fills it to check.
MATH.G3.MEASUR.CAPACITY.ESTIMATE_LITRES.hands_on: Estimating and then filling containers is done in class.

forms: how many minutes from one number to the next
how many minutes in an hour
MATH.G3.MEASUR.TIME.MINUTE_UNIT.mastery: The child knows the small marks on the clock face are minutes, that the minute hand moves from one number to the next in 5 minutes and round the whole face in 60 minutes (one hour), and names activities that take about a minute.

forms: quarter past, half past, quarter to
match a clock to a time
MATH.G3.MEASUR.TIME.TELL_PAST_TO.mastery: The child reads an analogue clock to the nearest five minutes and says the time with 'past' when the minute hand is on the right half (10 past 4) and 'to' when it is on the left half (20 to 5), naming the hour the short hand has passed or is coming to.

forms: which clock shows the same time
MATH.G3.MEASUR.TIME.READ_DIGITAL.mastery: The child reads a digital clock (7:45) as hours then minutes, says it in words, and matches it to the same time on an analogue clock (quarter to 8).

MATH.G3.MEASUR.TIME.WRITE_PAST_TO.mastery: The child writes the time shown on a clock in words with past or to (twenty-five past three, quarter to six), and draws the hands for a written time.

forms: more or less than an hour
MATH.G3.MEASUR.TIME.ESTIMATE_HOURS.mastery: The child estimates how many hours an everyday activity takes (a school day about 7 hours, a journey to town about 2 hours, a meal less than 1 hour) and picks the sensible estimate.

MATH.G3.MEASUR.TIME.ADD_TIME.mastery: The child adds times given in hours and minutes where the minutes total less than 60 (2 h 15 min + 1 h 30 min = 3 h 45 min), hours with hours and minutes with minutes, in stories and in columns.

MATH.G3.MEASUR.TIME.SUBTRACT_TIME.mastery: The child subtracts times in hours and minutes where no minutes need borrowing (3 h 50 min - 1 h 20 min = 2 h 30 min), hours from hours and minutes from minutes.

MATH.G3.MEASUR.MONEY.IDENTIFY_NOTES.mastery: The child names the Kenyan notes of sh. 50, 100, 200, 500 and 1,000 by their value (from the number, colour and size), sorts notes by value, and tells notes from coins.

MATH.G3.MEASUR.MONEY.COUNT_MONEY.mastery: The child counts a mix of notes and coins up to sh. 1,000 by starting with the largest and counting on in its value (500, 700, 800, 850, 870), and writes the total with sh.

MATH.G3.MEASUR.MONEY.ADD_MONEY.mastery: The child adds amounts of money up to sh. 1,000 (sh. 350 + sh. 275), with single regrouping, in shopping stories and in columns, and writes sh.

MATH.G3.MEASUR.MONEY.SUBTRACT_MONEY.mastery: The child subtracts amounts of money up to sh. 1,000 (what is left after spending, how much more one item costs), with single regrouping, and writes sh.

forms: how many of a note make the amount
MATH.G3.MEASUR.MONEY.SAME_AMOUNT_WAYS.mastery: The child shows one amount (sh. 200) in two or more ways (one sh. 200 note; two sh. 100 notes; four sh. 50 notes) and says whether two collections are worth the same.

forms: how many of a smaller note
what is missing in the change
MATH.G3.MEASUR.MONEY.CHANGE_DENOMINATION.mastery: The child changes a note into smaller notes or coins (a sh. 1,000 note into sh. 500 notes, a sh. 100 note into sh. 20 coins) and says how many of the smaller kind are given.

forms: role play at the model shop
MATH.G3.MEASUR.MONEY.BUY_WITH_BALANCE.mastery: The child finds the total cost of up to 3 items, takes it from the money paid, and gives the balance (change), within sh. 1,000, and checks that cost plus balance equals the money paid.

forms: where do you end after the steps
how many steps from the start
move forward or back on a path
MATH.G3.GEOMET.POSITION_AND_DIRECTION.MO.mastery: The child moves (or moves a counter on a grid) a given number of steps along a straight line from a stated starting point, forwards or backwards, and says where they end up and how many steps they moved.
MATH.G3.GEOMET.POSITION_AND_DIRECTION.MO.hands_on: Moving along lines outside the classroom is done in class.

forms: right or left of the person in the picture
MATH.G3.GEOMET.POSITION_AND_DIRECTION.LE.mastery: The child says which objects are on their right and left, and on the right or left of a person facing them or facing another way, using the person's own right and left.

forms: what do you face after turning right
turn left or right to reach a place
MATH.G3.GEOMET.POSITION_AND_DIRECTION.TU.mastery: The child moves straight from a point, turns a quarter turn to the right or the left, and says what they now face or which way they now go; in pictures and on paths, they follow a route of moves and turns.

forms: find the shape in an object
MATH.G3.GEOMET.SHAPES.NAME_SHAPES.mastery: The child names a rectangle, a square, a triangle, a circle and an oval from cut-outs, drawings and objects, in any position or size, by their sides and corners (a triangle has 3 sides), not by how they are turned.

forms: name the top and bottom shape
which picture is a triangle and a square
MATH.G3.GEOMET.SHAPES.SHAPES_IN_COMBINED.mastery: Given a combined shape (a hut, a house, an ice cream cone) the child names the two shapes it is made of and points to where one ends and the other begins.

MATH.G3.GEOMET.SHAPES.DRAW_COMBINED.mastery: The child draws a combined shape of two named shapes (a triangle on top of a square for a house), with the shapes sharing an edge and each shape drawn with the right number of sides.
MATH.G3.GEOMET.SHAPES.DRAW_COMBINED.hands_on: Drawing combined shapes is done in class, with the teacher checking the drawings.

MATH.G3.GEOMET.SHAPES.MODEL_COMBINED.mastery: The child makes a combined shape of two shapes from paper cut-outs, sticks or clay (a rectangle and a triangle for a hut) and names the two parts.
MATH.G3.GEOMET.SHAPES.MODEL_COMBINED.hands_on: Modelling with local materials is done in class.
